supplement.where: Appendices A to I at the end of the same PDF (pp. 11-25)
supplement.holds: Proofs (A), human baseline datasets and Tables 1-4 (B), prompts and generation protocols (C), kernel definitions (D), full numeric semantic benchmark Table 6 with 95% bootstrap CIs (E), rarefaction drift Table 7 (F), critical-benefit Table 8 (G), kernel robustness numbers (H), persona-mixture Table 9 and temperature Table 10 (I). No data or code URL is given.

paper_design_summary: The authors generate 50 outputs per task condition from three LLMs (GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash; neutral prompt, temperature 1.0) and compare the mean pairwise similarity of these model-only outputs with that of matched unaided human outputs. The human baselines are 87 WritingPrompts stories, 3,047 alternative-uses ideas from 109 socialmuse contributors, and 659 smartphone slogans from 95 Prolific participants. No person uses AI; the outcome is a human-relative diversity ratio (rho) and an excess-crowding coefficient (Delta) per model and task, with persona-mixture and temperature variants as model-only comparisons.

studies.label: Short stories (WritingPrompts baseline vs. three LLMs)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance; model-only generations were compared with unaided human baselines.
assignment.quote: We introduce a human-relative framework for benchmarking AI-induced human diversity collapse without requiring human–AI interaction data
assignment.locator: p. 1, Abstract; pp. 5-6, Section 4; pp. 12-14, Appendix B
assignment.prereg_locator: Not stated in the full text (pp. 1-29); benchmark design in pp. 5-6, Section 4, and baseline procedures in pp. 12-14, Appendix B.

participants.who: Corpus: 87 human-written stories, one per author, from Reddit r/WritingPrompts (WritingPrompts corpus), for three prompts with 35, 32, and 20 stories. No AI use by the writers.
participants.quote: These prompts provide 87 human-contributed stories, one per author.

ai_tool.how_used: Model-only generation: each model writes one story per request, 50 generations per prompt, neutral prompt at T = 1.0 (variants: temperature grid and 32-persona mixture). No human interaction.

task.description: Three ~100-word micro-fiction prompts (horror story, parachute failure, a character's 100-year life and last 10 seconds)

outcomes.name: Human-relative diversity ratio (rho), stories
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean off-diagonal pairwise semantic crowding (1 + cosine)/2 with sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings; rho = (1 - kappa_A)/(1 - kappa_H), rho < 1 means AI outputs less diverse than humans; matched-sample bootstrap, equal-weight average over 3 prompts. Model side: 50 generations per prompt per model. n_units = human stories. Primary semantic method: p. 6, Section 4, Eqs. 12-13; p. 16, Appendix D. Robustness variant (plot-synopsis kernel): Robustness kernel: one-sentence plot synopses generated by GPT-5.4 (T = 0), embedded with all-mpnet-base-v2; same rho. CIs only in Figure 6. These are alternative kernels for the same diversity outcome (pp. 16-17, Appendix D.1; p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 19-20, Appendix H.1 and Figure 6).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLM-generated stories (each of GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash; neutral prompt, T = 1.0)
contrasts.reported: Stories: GPT-5.4 kappa_H 0.706, kappa_A 0.892, Delta 0.186, rho 0.372 [0.338, 0.408]; Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.706, 0.857, 0.151, rho 0.485 [0.441, 0.533]; Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.705, 0.869, 0.164, rho 0.446 [0.406, 0.490] (95% percentile bootstrap CI for rho). Direction refers to diversity (rho < 1). Robustness (plot-synopsis kernel): GPT-5.4 moves from rho = 0.372 to 0.509, Claude Sonnet 4.5 from 0.485 to 0.594, and Gemini 2.5 Flash from 0.446 to 0.519 (full-text to plot-synopsis kernel); all remain below parity.
contrasts.locator: p. 18, Table 6; p. 6, Figure 1; p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 19-20, Appendix H.1, Figure 6

diversity_detail.metric: Mean off-diagonal pairwise crowding kappa, summarized as rho = (1 - kappa_A)/(1 - kappa_H) and Delta = max{0, kappa_A - kappa_H} (p. 4, Eqs. 1-3; p. 6, Eq. 13). The primary semantic kernel is (1 + cosine(f(x), f(y)))/2 (p. 6, Eq. 12). The plot-synopsis robustness kernel applies the same cosine-based kernel to story synopses (p. 17, Eq. 15).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2, with normalized embeddings, for the primary full-story and plot-synopsis kernels (p. 16, Appendix D; p. 17, Appendix D.1). Synopses are generated by GPT-5.4 at T = 0 (p. 16, Appendix D.1).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Within each of the three story-prompt conditions, each bootstrap draw samples b = min{n_H, n_A} human author/story units and b model generations with replacement. Mean crowding uses all off-diagonal pairs separately within the human draw and within the model draw. Rho and Delta are calculated within condition, then averaged with equal weights across prompts (p. 6, Section 4; p. 13, Table 1).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap intervals for rho using the matched-sample procedure (p. 6, Section 4; p. 18, Table 6). Plot-synopsis interval bounds are shown graphically in p. 20, Figure 6, without printed numeric endpoints.
diversity_detail.notes: Higher rho means greater diversity relative to humans; rho < 1 means model outputs are less diverse. Higher kappa and Delta mean more crowding (p. 4, Section 3.1). Plot-synopsis results are a robustness variant of the same outcome (p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 19-20, Appendix H.1). Duplicate stories are retained; duplicate texts are summarized once and mapped back to all corresponding rows for the synopsis analysis (p. 16, Appendix D.1).

studies.label: Alternative Uses Task (socialmuse baseline vs. three LLMs)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance; model-only generations were compared with unaided human baselines.
assignment.quote: We introduce a human-relative framework for benchmarking AI-induced human diversity collapse without requiring human–AI interaction data
assignment.locator: p. 1, Abstract; pp. 5-6, Section 4; pp. 12-14, Appendix B
assignment.prereg_locator: Not stated in the full text (pp. 1-29); benchmark design in pp. 5-6, Section 4, and baseline procedures in pp. 12-14, Appendix B.

participants.who: Existing dataset (socialmuse, Baten et al.): 109 human contributors who generated 3,047 unaided alternative-use ideas for five objects (shoe, button, key, wooden pencil, automobile tire). Only unaided ideas retained.
participants.quote: The retained human baseline contains 109 participants, 5 object conditions, and 3,047 unaided ideas (see Table 2).
participants.locator: p. 13, Appendix B.2 and Table 2; p. 5, Section 4

ai_tool.how_used: Model-only generation: one alternative use per request, 50 generations per object per model, neutral prompt at T = 1.0. No human interaction.

task.description: Alternative uses for five common objects, excluding the primary use

outcomes.name: Human-relative diversity ratio (rho), AUT
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same semantic kernel and rho as S1-O1; participant-aware bootstrap (sample a participant, then one response); equal-weight average over five objects. n_units = human ideas (109 participants). Primary semantic method: p. 6, Section 4, Eqs. 12-13; p. 16, Appendix D. Robustness variant (concept-bucket kernel): Kernel = 1 if two responses fall in the same concept bucket; buckets assigned by the MuseScorer retrieval-assisted LLM pipeline (llama3.3:70b-Instruct judge, all-mpnet-base-v2 retrieval, K_c = 10). These are alternative kernels for the same diversity outcome (p. 17, Appendix D.2; p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 20-21, Appendix H.3; p. 23, Figure 11).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLM-generated alternative uses (each of GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash; neutral prompt, T = 1.0)
contrasts.reported: AUT: GPT-5.4 kappa_H 0.601, kappa_A 0.791, Delta 0.190, rho 0.525 [0.499, 0.548]; Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.601, 0.877, 0.275, rho 0.309 [0.277, 0.340]; Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.601, 0.743, 0.142, rho 0.645 [0.612, 0.677] (95% percentile bootstrap CI for rho). Robustness (concept-bucket kernel): GPT-5.4 has rho = 0.866 with 95% CI [0.833, 0.894], Claude Sonnet 4.5 has rho = 0.715 with 95% CI [0.665, 0.759], and Gemini 2.5 Flash has rho = 0.938 with 95% CI [0.920, 0.953].
contrasts.locator: p. 18, Table 6; p. 6, Figure 1; pp. 20-21, Appendix H.3; p. 23, Figure 11; p. 8, Section 5.4

diversity_detail.metric: Mean off-diagonal pairwise crowding kappa, summarized as rho = (1 - kappa_A)/(1 - kappa_H) and Delta = max{0, kappa_A - kappa_H} (p. 4, Eqs. 1-3; p. 6, Eq. 13). The primary semantic kernel is (1 + cosine(f(x), f(y)))/2 (p. 6, Eq. 12). The concept-bucket robustness kernel equals 1 for two responses assigned to the same object-specific concept bucket and 0 otherwise (p. 17, Eq. 16).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 with normalized embeddings for the primary semantic kernel (p. 16, Appendix D). The same model provides nearest-neighbor retrieval for the MuseScorer concept-bucketing pipeline, whose LLM judge is llama3.3:70b-Instruct with K_c = 10 comparison candidates (p. 17, Appendix D.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Within each of five object conditions, each bootstrap draw samples b = min{n_H, n_A} human participants and b model generations with replacement, then one response per selected participant. Mean crowding uses all off-diagonal pairs separately within the human responses and within the model generations. Rho and Delta are calculated within object, then averaged with equal weights across objects (p. 6, Section 4; p. 13, Appendix B.2 and Table 2).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap intervals for rho, with participants sampled first and one response sampled per selected participant (p. 6, Section 4; p. 18, Table 6). Concept-bucket intervals are printed in pp. 20-21, Appendix H.3, and plotted in p. 23, Figure 11.
diversity_detail.notes: Higher rho means greater diversity relative to humans; rho < 1 means model outputs are less diverse. Higher kappa and Delta mean more crowding (p. 4, Section 3.1). Concept-bucket results are a robustness variant of the same outcome (p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 20-21, Appendix H.3). Human and model responses, including protocol variants, are pooled within object to construct the concept codebook; the subsequent crowding estimates are within each source. Exact duplicate responses are retained (p. 17, Appendix D.2).

studies.label: Smartphone marketing slogans (new Prolific baseline vs. three LLMs)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance; model-only generations were compared with unaided human baselines.
assignment.quote: We introduce a human-relative framework for benchmarking AI-induced human diversity collapse without requiring human–AI interaction data

participants.who: U.S.-based Prolific participants in an IRB-approved online study who wrote unaided slogans for a hypothetical new smartphone (3 minutes, at least 3 slogans, at most 6 words each); 659 slogans, 650 unique. No AI use.
participants.quote: The retained dataset contains 659 slogans from 95 participants, of which 650 are unique strings (see Table 4).

ai_tool.how_used: Model-only generation: one slogan per request, 50 generations per model, neutral prompt at T = 1.0. No human interaction.

task.description: Creative marketing slogans (max 6 words) for a new smartphone

outcomes.name: Human-relative diversity ratio (rho), slogans
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same semantic kernel and rho as S1-O1; participant-aware bootstrap. n_units = human slogans (95 participants). Primary semantic method: p. 6, Section 4, Eqs. 12-13; p. 16, Appendix D. Robustness variant (lexical-template kernels): Non-stopword token Jaccard and character-trigram Jaccard on normalized slogans. Numbers printed only for GPT-5.4; Claude and Gemini only in Figure 8. These are alternative kernels for the same diversity outcome (pp. 17-18, Appendix D.3; p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 20-21, Appendix H.2 and Figure 8).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLM-generated slogans (each of GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash; neutral prompt, T = 1.0)
contrasts.reported: Slogans: GPT-5.4 kappa_H 0.597, kappa_A 0.928, Delta 0.331, rho 0.179 [0.096, 0.275]; Claude Sonnet 4.5 0.597, 0.729, 0.132, rho 0.672 [0.596, 0.734]; Gemini 2.5 Flash 0.597, 0.733, 0.136, rho 0.662 [0.562, 0.746] (95% percentile bootstrap CI for rho). Robustness (lexical-template kernels): GPT-5.4 shows substantial lexical crowding, with rho = 0.368 under non-stopword Jaccard and rho = 0.305 under character-trigram Jaccard; Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash lexical rho values remain below one (Figure 8 only).
contrasts.locator: p. 18, Table 6; p. 6, Figure 1; p. 7, Section 5.1; p. 8, Section 5.4; p. 21, Figure 8

diversity_detail.metric: Mean off-diagonal pairwise crowding kappa, summarized as rho = (1 - kappa_A)/(1 - kappa_H) and Delta = max{0, kappa_A - kappa_H} (p. 4, Eqs. 1-3; p. 6, Eq. 13). The primary semantic kernel is (1 + cosine(f(x), f(y)))/2 (p. 6, Eq. 12). Lexical-template robustness kernels use non-stopword token Jaccard similarity and character-trigram Jaccard similarity on lowercased slogans with normalized punctuation and whitespace (pp. 17-18, Appendix D.3, Eqs. 17-18).
diversity_detail.embedding_model: sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 with normalized embeddings for the primary semantic kernel (p. 16, Appendix D); no embedding model for either Jaccard kernel (pp. 17-18, Appendix D.3).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Within the smartphone slogan condition, each bootstrap draw samples b = min{n_H, n_A} human participants and b model generations with replacement, then one slogan per selected participant. Mean crowding uses all off-diagonal pairs separately within human slogans and within model slogans, from which rho and Delta are calculated (p. 6, Section 4; pp. 13-14, Appendix B.3 and Table 4).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap intervals for rho, with participants sampled first and one slogan sampled per selected participant (p. 6, Section 4; p. 18, Table 6). Lexical-kernel intervals are shown graphically in p. 21, Figure 8, without printed numeric endpoints.
diversity_detail.notes: Higher rho means greater diversity relative to humans; rho < 1 means model outputs are less diverse. Higher kappa and Delta mean more crowding (p. 4, Section 3.1). The two lexical-template kernels are robustness variants of the same outcome (p. 8, Section 5.4; pp. 20-21, Appendix H.2). Duplicate slogans are retained as part of the human crowding baseline (p. 13, Appendix B.3).

eligibility.reason: No person receives AI help: model-only generations are compared with unaided human outputs, without human-AI interaction data (p. 1, Abstract; pp. 5-6, Section 4). Criterion 1 is not met. Criterion 2 is met by 109 analyzed AUT participants in S2 (p. 13, Appendix B.2 and Table 2) and 95 analyzed slogan participants in S3 (pp. 13-14, Appendix B.3 and Table 4). Criterion 3 is met because diversity is computed on produced outputs using within-source pairwise crowding (p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 6, Section 4, Eqs. 12-13). Core remains no and context_class remains ai_vs_human; persona and temperature variants are model-only comparisons.

one_line_finding: Under the neutral main protocol (neutral prompt, T = 1.0) and primary semantic kernel, all nine model-task combinations (GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash on stories, AUT, and slogans) were less diverse than matched unaided human baselines, with human-relative diversity ratios from 0.179 (GPT-5.4, slogans) to 0.672 (Claude Sonnet 4.5, slogans) and every 95% bootstrap upper bound below 1 (p. 18, Table 6; p. 6, Figure 1).
notes: Table 9 (p. 23) prints main-protocol rho values that differ slightly from Table 6 for four cells (AUT GPT-5.4 0.526 vs 0.525; Slogans Claude 0.673 vs 0.672; Slogans Gemini 0.660 vs 0.662; Stories Claude 0.486 vs 0.485); Table 6 values are recorded. Persona-mixture prompting raises rho in eight of nine model-task cells (p. 8; p. 23, Table 9), a model-only comparison not coded as an outcome.
